name: Northwind Orders API
technology: bearer-token sign-in answering JSON rather than a cookie; X-CSRF-Token header convention; one HTML page over a JSON API

design.engine: QA NXT form and page test engine (deterministic)

untested: authz.missing on /: Inconclusive: The route answered 200 to an anonymous caller, but with no data in it (only 33 characters of visible text — an application shell). An application that renders in the browser serves the same shell on every route and fetches its data separately, so this route cannot show an exposure. Check the endpoints it calls.

auth.reset-reuse on http://127.0.0.1:4500/api/auth/token: Inconclusive: The reset token is not returned in the response, which is correct behaviour for a real application. Reuse cannot be tested without the token, so this is reported as not testable by this check rather than as a pass.
auth.session-lifetime on http://127.0.0.1:4500/api/auth/token: Inconclusive: Sign-in failed (404).
auth.session-logout on http://127.0.0.1:4500/api/auth/token: Inconclusive: The session did not authenticate even before sign-out (404).
authz.missing on http://127.0.0.1:4500/api/auth/token: Inconclusive: The owner could not read it either (404).

authz.readonly on http://127.0.0.1:4500/api/auth/token: Inconclusive: Not evaluated: alice could not write either — it answered 401. An account that is permitted to write has to succeed before a refusal for one that is not means anything.

request.csrf on http://127.0.0.1:4500/api/auth/token: Inconclusive: Not evaluated: alice authenticates with a bearer token and the application set no session cookie. A browser attaches a cookie to a cross-site request on its own, which is what makes forgery possible; it does not attach a bearer token, which only the application's own code sets. So there is no cross-site request here for an anti-forgery token to defend. That is a property of how this application authenticates, not a gap in the scan.

request.origin on http://127.0.0.1:4500/api/auth/token: Inconclusive: Not evaluated: alice authenticates with a bearer token and the application set no session cookie. A browser attaches a cookie to a cross-site request on its own, which is what makes forgery possible; it does not attach a bearer token, which only the application's own code sets. So varying the origin would compare two requests neither of which carries credentials. That is a property of how this application authenticates, not a gap in the scan.
xss.stored on http://127.0.0.1:4500/api/auth/token: Inconclusive: No field was discovered on this page to store a marker in.
